threads.body: I'd guess that the JIT would optimize this allocation away, did you happen to run a benchmark it?

replies.body: Thanks for the pointer... after your comment, I ran a JMH benchmark with -prof gc on JDK 25, matching 20 keys per op. With a `*` include, the for-each version allocated 1120 B/op because the iterator wasn't scalar-replaced. The index loop allocated 0 B/op and ran about 6× faster (5.5 → 32 ops/µs). With a multi-pattern selector the JIT does remove the iterator, so there the two loops are equal (4.8 vs 5.2 ops/µs, 0 B/op both). I can add the benchmark to instrumentation-api/src/jmh if you'd like it in? Or I can put the code in a gist?
oh, good find, sent https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/21324 to apply this in other places

A trailing * now returns true in globMatches(), so `*`, `foo*` and `foo?*` all skip scanning the rest of the value. I removed the special case from createGlobPredicate()
